habitat: Singly, in groups, or in large flocks in the shallows of coastal and inland waters, flooded fields and farmlands. A flock takes flight densely.
summary: An abundant summer visitor. The male is much larger than the female, the reeve. The bill is short and slightly decurved with a bulbous tip, the face is plain except for a small white patch at the bill base, and the upperparts are boldly scaled. Adult legs are orange and immature legs are grey-green. In flight, white ovals show beside the dark tail. Newman does not name the months. The Kemp name Ruff and the code NB were left unchanged.

bill.shape: Short and slightly decurved, with a slightly bulbous tip. The colour is not given.

head.pattern: The face is featureless except for a small white patch at the base of the bill. The head and rear of the neck are dappled light brown.

upperparts.pattern: Back and wings dark brown, with every feather boldly edged white. The upperparts are boldly scaled or mottled.

wings.pattern: Dark brown wings with feathers boldly edged white.

tail.shape: In flight, white oval patches show on the sides of the dark tail.

calls.description: Birds in a flock may call 'chit' in a twittering chorus. No grade A or grade B recording from South Africa was found. The selected file is a grade A call from Poland. The filename is XC233522-Phillomaus_pugnax_Poland_Jarek_Matusiak_20150329_04.mp3.

research.note: Newman calls it an abundant summer visitor and does not name the months, so status is summer-migrant and monthsPresent is unset. Immature legs are grey-green, so that colour is not stored as one vocabulary name. A male may show traces of breeding plumage in spring or autumn, but those colours are not listed. No grade A or grade B recording from South Africa was found. The iNaturalist account has no display name, so the login jandutoit is credited. The Kemp code NB was left unchanged.
